before.name: Waptus River and the PCT, then the Shovel Creek fisherman's trail to the foot of the slab
before.notes:
From the Salmon La Sac trailhead, hike the Waptus River Trail about nine miles to Waptus Lake. The hiker bridge over Spinola Creek near the lake has washed out, so cross at the nearby horse ford, reached from the Waptus Pass Trail. Where the trail joins the PCT, head southbound (west).

Shortly before the PCT crosses the Waptus River, leave the trail and head northwest toward a faint shoulder and bench through flat, easy forest. Pick up a fisherman's trail on the southwest side of that bench and follow it toward Shovel Creek, then up and over the bench past an informal campsite with a giant cairn, where it starts to climb the shoulder on the east side of Shovel Creek.

Before long the trail leaves the forest straight onto talus. Easy talus walking brings you to Shovel Creek; cross where convenient.

Roughly 13 miles to the base, five to six hours. Most parties camp near the Waptus River PCT bridge.
before.season: July to September; documented ascents cluster in August
hazards: About 2,000 ft of unprotected friction slab, mostly climbed unroped
Rock quality deteriorating markedly on the final three summit-block pitches
No water on the slab — carry the whole climbing day's supply
A long, remote approach with no confirmed cell coverage
The Shovel Lake descent alternative involves loose dirt high, brush and cliff bands low, and heavy route-finding
before.baseFinding:
Crossing Shovel Creek off the talus puts you at the foot of the Mega Slab — that is the arrival, and it is a creek crossing rather than a judgement. The slab drops from the peak's southeast shoulder at about 6,700 ft all the way to Shovel Creek at about 3,700 ft, so there is no ambiguity about which piece of rock it is: it is the enormous unbroken sheet above you, one of the longest continuous sandstone slabs in North America.

Which line on the slab is the real question here, and for this route the answer is a single word: lowest. Infinite Beauty begins at the lowest part of the slab, on a shallow rib. Walk the base downhill until it stops going down, and start on the rib there.

How that distinguishes it from its neighbour: Timeless Treasure climbs the middle of the slab. So if you have walked out along the base looking for a nicer-looking start, you are on Timeless Treasure. The lowest point is the whole distinction and it is decidable by walking downhill rather than by looking.

What the rock should feel like, as confirmation: clean, solid, grippy low-angle stone with minimal breaks, and roughly 2,000 ft of sustained fourth class. Approach shoes or trail runners friction well on it and most of the slab is climbed unroped. If you are pulling into cracks or dodging vegetation, you are off the clean sheet.

And where the route ends its own identity: after about 2,000 ft the line naturally angles right and joins Timeless Treasure for brief, unexposed low-fifth moves up overlaps trending up and right to the southeast shoulder. Easy scrambling then leads to the summit block, where the rock quality noticeably deteriorates over the final three pitches.

before: Ten stoppers, two small cams, and six runners were adequate for the whole route on one recorded ascent. A single 50m rope is enough for the rappels, but 60m or two 50m ropes let 3-person parties reach belay stances more comfortably.

before.notes: Sustained 4th-class climbing on clean, low-angle sandstone up the center of the slab, left of the giant corner.
3 pitches combined to the summit; rock quality noticeably worse than on the slab below; shares the same finish as Infinite Beauty.

before.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
before.note: Standard access to the Core Enchantments via Colchuck Lake and Aasgard Pass.
before.directions: From US-2 at the western edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FS Road 7601) and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park and overnight trips May 15 to Oct 31 need an Enchantment permit; the road is usually gated November into May.

before.name: Gnome Tarn
before.note: Landmark tarn on the boot path leading to the base of Prusik Peak's south face routes.
before.directions: Take the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles to the Colchuck Lake Trail, cross Mountaineer Creek and climb to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft. From the boulder field at the lake's south end, climb Aasgard Pass, about 2,000 ft of loose scree in 1.25 miles, then cross the Core past Tranquil and Isolation lakes and go cross-country north over slabs and talus to Gnome Tarn below Prusik's south face.

before.name: Prusik Peak south face base
before.directions: Walk up from the tarn to the foot of the south face and find two large V-shaped features; the route starts in the chimney immediately left of them, to the right of the classic line in the middle of the face.

before.name: Prusik Peak
before.note: South Face route, 6-7 pitches, FA Beckey-Davis 1962.
before.directions: Climb seven pitches, about 650 ft: left out of the chimney onto knobs, up face and cracks to Snafflehound Ledge, traverse right, take the 5.9 dihedral crux, then the crack and gully past a chockstone to the notch east of the summit horn, finishing with a friction traverse and jam crack to the summit.
